newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Astra says to appeal German Losec ruling. [CORRECTED 10:14 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Astra says to appeal German Losec ruling. [CORRECTED 10:14 GMT]

text.p: Swedish drugs group Astra said on Thursday it would appeal a ruling by Germany's federal patent court (corrects from "...a ruling by the German Supreme Court...") that said Astra's anti-ulcer drug Losec was not covered by the German Supplementary Protection Certificate (SPC) rules.
The European Union (EU) adopted the SPC in 1993 to compensate the research-based pharmaceutical industry for the long development time and regulatory approval procedures, Astra said in a statement.
Astra applied for an SPC for omeprazole, the substance in Losec, in the European countries concerned and was granted an SPC in Germany until early 2003.

"The German generics company Ratiopharm has challenged the validity of this SPC in Germany on formal grounds and has received support for its claim in Germany's federal patent court in Munich," Astra said.
"According to the court, Astra's Losec is not covered by the German SPC rules."
Astra said it would appeal the ruling to the German Supreme court and request a ruling by the European Court of Justice.

"In Astra's view the SPC for Losec is also valid in Germany," the company said. "If the patent court's ruling is nevertheless upheld, the substance patent for omeprazole in Germany will expire -- as originally -- in April 1999."
In other major European markets the SPCs for omeprazole is also covered by a number of other patents which expire on different later dates, Astra said.
